texts: good. the roosting comes through as a fireable generic rule over sky-cats, with the cliff-spires as its place and 'during the day' carried as the time.
good. the denial is carried as a rule over sky-cats at strength zero while the village stays a real referent — exactly the shape a negated generic should take.

bad: 'the Keepers' is a capitalized plural name, so it should stand for one named body; the parse instead invents a group of people typed `keeper` and adds a rule making every one of them tolerate sky-cats, which your sentence never says. Say which reading you want — for the per-member one write "Each of the Keepers tolerates sky-cats."; if you mean the Keepers acting as a single body, the sentence can stand as it is, but it must yield one tolerating and no per-member claims.
